[NCBK.2.8] **Every fault is a stream event.** The four fault classes reach the integrator through the
stream callback like any other observable event, in `seq` order, and take four
kinds of their own:

| Kind | Value | Raised when |
|---|---|---|
| `DS_EV_TYPE_ERROR`   | 21 | a value is present and the operation is invalid at that site; the activation is abandoned |
| `DS_EV_BOUNDS_ERROR` | 22 | a **declared** cap was reached; the operation is rejected and the engine is intact |
| `DS_EV_ENGINE_ERROR` | 23 | engine state is no longer trustworthy; the tier halts ([NCBK.2.9]) |
| `DS_EV_COMPUTATION_ERROR` | 24 | a well-typed operation has no answer — `DIVIDE_BY_ZERO`, `DOMAIN`, `NOT_REPRESENTABLE` ([LERR.1.4.9]); the activation is abandoned |

**Four kinds and not one**, because the recorded form is four atoms, and a single kind carrying a
discriminator would have a C consumer switching on a payload field where a
replayer switches on the atom. Two discriminators for one distinction is what
drifts.

**`ComputationError` takes a kind.** It is
a fault under the same rule as the other three and carries the same disposition
as a TypeError, so a vocabulary with a disposition and no kind would leave an
integrator able to observe one and not the other. The first sentence of this
clause admits no such exception: *every* fault is a stream event.

**The disposition is the kind.** A TypeError and a ComputationError always
abandon the activation, a BoundsError always leaves the engine intact, an
EngineError always halts — so none of the four carries a recoverability or
disposition field, and a consumer reads it off the kind.

⚠ **A fault reaching the callback does not mean it was persisted.** The engine
emits; whether the event reaches durable storage is the integrator's, and for a
recorder failure it by definition does not. The engine writes nothing itself
([IARC.1.14]), so this is a property of the integrator's sink rather than of the
event.
